latest_nl_proof:
Assume that for every real number t we have f(t+1)=f(t). We prove the conclusion by induction on m ∈ ℕ.

Define P(m) to be the statement: for every real number x, f(x-(m:ℝ))=f(x).

Base case m=0: for every real x, f(x-(0:ℝ))=f(x), which is just f(x)=f(x).

Inductive step: assume P(m) holds for some m ∈ ℕ. Let x be any real number. Apply the hypothesis f(t+1)=f(t) with t = x-(m:ℝ)-1. Then
f((x-(m:ℝ)-1)+1)=f(x-(m:ℝ)-1),
so f(x-(m:ℝ))=f(x-(m:ℝ)-1). By the induction hypothesis applied to the real number x-1, we have f((x-1)-(m:ℝ))=f(x-1), i.e. f(x-(m:ℝ)-1)=f(x-1). Also, applying the induction hypothesis directly to x gives f(x-(m:ℝ))=f(x). Combining these equalities yields
f(x-((m+1):ℝ))=f(x).
Thus P(m+1) holds.

Therefore P(m) is true for all natural numbers m. Hence for every real x and every natural m, f(x-(m:ℝ))=f(x).

statement_nl: If for every real number x one has f(x + 1) = f(x), then for every real number x and every natural number m, f(x - (m : ℝ)) = f(x).

domain_restrictions: f is defined for all real inputs (so x plus 1 and x minus m are valid inputs)
m is a natural number and is coerced to an integer amount for subtraction from x
subtraction by m uses the real number obtained from m
